title: Prove correlated dirt is necessary at P104 wire meetings (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped response-space proof with an exact finite local construction, answering a boundary subproblem of Matarener's #6217 one-helper wire question. An independently dirty helper cannot supply the missing effective source when both other incoming rows are clean. Correlated dirt must reach at least two of the three inputs. If exactly two carry it, the remaining clean row must isolate the exceptional A2 vertex; each dirty row must carry at least seven of the other 23 live coordinates under the 16-port cap. No new κ.

```text
three incoming rows, one dirty column
  -> two-dimensional dirt-free kernel
  -> isolated dirt impossible under the support cap
  -> correlated pair + exceptional singleton admits a local response word
```

The new four-event dyadic word at labels 11,19,487 produces both required Gram response rows and preserves its helper entrance value dX+h. The original helper value h is not restored by this meeting. This is a response projection, not a complete arbitrary-public-input endpoint or a complete one-helper program.

Only `research/p104-wire-dirty-entry/` is added. Scientific base and refreshed canonical main are `2485805a6d47f36ea83ddde6327d453ac82d44dc`, priority revision 8, selected conditional κ .003125804. The selected frontier is unchanged. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19292022).

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Matarener / #6217 for the question and sign/capacity/content premises, DreamingOfClouds / #6170 for frame-contract context, and their retained P104/native/helper/controller/caller lineage. Classical kernel, support and row-operation facts retain their classical status. No predecessor scientific executable is imported or audited.

## Evidence

Before: the source requires a third incoming source and leaves the one-helper route open. After: the new proof identifies a necessary dirty-entry pattern and supplies one local response attainer for that changed entry.

- Exact forward and inverse checks cover all 25 projected input columns, plus 625 scalar dirty-input fixtures.
- Every one of 251,559 normalized F3 cases is checked by both kernel-image arithmetic and separately implemented augmented-row elimination. Feasible counts at dirt-support sizes 1,2,3 are 0,288,108, respectively. These are counts in the stated four-live-coordinate regression domain, not a P104 program census.
- Eleven semantic/invalid-event controls reject; two outside-scope positive controls explain the support and nonzero-dirt hypotheses.
- Warning-strict development-mode normal and optimized direct checks pass in 3.49 and 3.55 seconds locally. Both registered commands pass, including their current source-hash receipts, well below five minutes each.
- Committed bytes, modes and full declared source ancestry pass at `1866c2f3ee2d4cf5bf3e8f008883a6605ab10ed3`. Official export/input integrity passes. Both read-only Git-free replay modes pass with empty PATH; all eight exported files retain their bytes and modes. Two exported source corruptions and two semantic corruptions reject.

From the repository root, reproduce with CPython 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -X dev -B research/p104-wire-dirty-entry/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -X dev -B -O research/p104-wire-dirty-entry/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-wire-dirty-entry
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/p104-wire-dirty-entry --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 can replace the absolute interpreter path. Expected markers are `PASS_P104_WIRE_DIRTY_ENTRY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Receipts are generated, with package/input hashes; none is handwritten.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal result is the written support/kernel proof over characteristic different from two. The source's sign and capacity claims are cited premises, not newly validated results. The exact P104 construction covers one meeting and only the live/one-dirt response projection. It requires prepared aX-h, dX+h and a singleton. It leaves dX in the helper and omits other public/dirty columns.

Preparation, complete original-input preservation, later cleanup, native availability, routing, precision/storage, stock, compiler closure, a complete signed invoice and an actual caller remain unproved. Unknown costs are not zero. No selected cold replay, predecessor scientific replay, Lean, Docker, native synthesis or full multiplication theorem check was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Can actual pre-cut public/helper trajectories prepare the correlated pair and exceptional singleton while preserving every original input column? First name the contact that deposits -h into a public register.
2. Can a legal later access remove dX and yield a complete bill below the matched two-helper route? Price all paid and productive histograms together before expanding construction.

## Related open work

- #6251: selected-word scalar ADD fusion; preserves the existing response contract rather than changing this meeting entrance.
- #6249: PR6167 numerical compiler-premise audit; does not establish this proposed local preparation or caller.
- #6248: separate descending-cache floors for reader 497; different frame and cache hypotheses.
- #6247: dyadic complex rank-seven approximation of the same P104 Gram object; this package requires exact local response rows.
- #5606: a complete prepared-owned split-helper proposal; this package uses correlated arbitrary dirt and supplies no completed supplier invoice.
- #5553: successor helper handoffs and target credits on a fixed word; does not construct the wire entry studied here.
- #3915: a fixed P104 flag's chronological coefficient transport; different ports and no common numerical comparison performed.
- #3907: a full correction source-lifetime floor in a fixed monotone grammar; this package proves a local entry condition, not a global lifetime count.
- #3894: a complete paid full-frame end-cut correction; its full invoice is outside this local meeting projection.

No additional computations were run to compare predecessor results. Live open PRs and reservations were rechecked immediately before committing; no matching wire-entry target was found within that bounded coverage.

- #6258: rounded native identity-cycle drift on P104 frame recipes; this package concerns exact rational response coefficients at one meeting and computes no rounded orbit.
- #6266: bounded-error partition cuts for framed circuits; its simultaneous symbol-success threshold differs from this exact dirt-free response-space condition.

Completion refresh inspected all 18 currently open PRs from this account, including those created since the advance CLAIM. The current open-title list was also refreshed. No new PR computes this same local dirty-entry census or response word, and no shared-number disagreement was identified. No additional predecessor computation was run.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/p104-wire-dirty-entry)`, passed at exact head `1866c2f3ee2d4cf5bf3e8f008883a6605ab10ed3` in [run 41049207445](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41049207445). The completed checks were read once; separate run metadata confirms the matching head, completed status and successful conclusion. All registered checks also passed locally. Hosted replay certifies the registered finite checks, not independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance of the universal proof. The delivered local scope matches the advance CLAIM.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: one isolated opt-in research package. No shared code, frozen predecessor, selected record or frontier changes.
